title: Democrats Missed Hegseth Impeachment Vote While at a Fundraiser with Defense Lobbyists
author: Ryan Grim
content:

Whip Katherine Clark, Elect Democratic Women chair Rep. Lois Frankel, and EDW
executive board member Rep. Julia Brownley attend the GRAMMYs on the Hill
Advocacy Day Awards Dinner on April 8, 2025 in Washington, D.C. Photo by Leigh
Vogel/Getty Images for The Recording Academy.

Maybe they waited too long for the cake pops to come back around.

After 11 Democrats missed the vote to impeach War Secretary Pete Hegseth on
Tuesday, an ill-timed Tuesday reception hosted by the political action
committee Elect Democratic Women (EDW) has become the focus of increasing
attention. According to an RSVP list of the event obtained by Drop Site News,
the party was studded with representatives of the country's top weapons makers
and the city's most powerful defense contractor lobbying firms.

A motion from Republicans to effectively kill the impeachment resolution
[passed 211-204](https://www.congress.gov/votes/house/119-2/317). Three of the
missing Democrats blamed their tardiness on traffic getting back to the
Capitol from an event.

The unexcused absences have sent an angry Democratic base, which was already
clamoring for leadership changes in the House and Senate and an end to the war
with Iran, all the way up the wall. The complete list of EDW partygoers is
unlikely to calm anyone down.

The event, billed as a "New Member Reception," was expected to be attended by
a slew of lobbyists for weapons makers, AI companies, crypto firms, insurance
companies, Big Pharma, and others looking to press their case for federal
largesse, according to the event RSVP list. EDW, chaired by Rep. **Lois
Frankel**(D-Fl.), served as a major pass-through for **AIPAC** cash in the
2026 cycle. AIPAC's super PAC **United Democracy Project** [funneled at least
](https://www.fec.gov/data/disbursements/?data_type=processed&committee_id=C00799031&recipient_name=C00685297&recipient_name=C00863472&two_year_transaction_period=2026)$2.35
million into EDW Action this year, according to federal campaign finance
records.

The event was to be attended, according to the list, by 132 lobbyists, The
defense industry was represented by at least two people from **Lockheed
Martin** , as well as representatives from top defense lobbying firms like
**Cornerstone Public Affairs** , **Invariant** , **Akin Gump** , **Porter
Group** , **Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck** , **K &L Gates**, and **BGR
Group**. AI and Big Tech were represented by lobbyists from **Anthropic** ,
**Google** , **Dell** , **Salesforce** , **Airbnb** , and **Intel**. Big
Pharma had people from **PhRMA** , **Genentech** , **AstraZeneca** , **Blue
Cross Blue Shield** , **CVS** , and **Elevance Health**. Prediction markets
were championed by a **Kalshi** lobbyist while cryptocurrencies were advocated
for by someone from **Coinbase**. And, for good measure, two lobbyists from
**Bayer-Monsanto** , the company responsible for releasing the cancer-causing
weed killer RoundUp, attended the bash. Major firms like **Walmart** ,
**Comcast** , and **Delta** were in attendance, as were a handful of major
unions.

The event ran from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. House leadership scheduled the vote to
impeach Hegseth at 5:30 p.m., and the vote closed at 6:05.

The "run of show" had Frankel giving remarks at 5:00, cutting it close to the
vote time, given rush hour traffic down Pennsylvania Avenue from the venue,
Goldfinch Social.

![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!iRge!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe2dfa675-6c89-4308-b233-4d270a465d9c_1888x444.png)

Reps. **[Julia
Brownley](https://x.com/ZachSchermele/status/2120589385426964910?a=aBrLt1lcWxruEuiMFjw&s=20)
**(D-Calif.), **Melanie Stansbury**(D-N.M.), and **Brittany
Pettersen**(D-Colo.) missed the vote and attended the event. Brownley is an
executive board member of EDW and Stansbury is a board member. Eight others
missed the vote-Reps. **Laura Gillen** , **Nancy Pelosi** , **Haley Stevens**
, **Marilyn Strickland** , **Frederica Wilson** , **Jonathan Jackson** ,
**Steven Horsford** , and **Lou Correa**. Pelosi said she was attending a
Veteran's Day event; Horsford cited a "personal emergency." Jackson made it to
the steps of the Capitol on time and was seen filming a social media video
before the vote was gaveled to a close, but inexplicably missed the vote. He
said he is taking "full accountability." Stevens was endorsed by EDW but was
thrown out of the Michigan Democratic Party for endorsing the Republican in
the Michigan Senate race. She has been hanging out in the Republican cloakroom
during votes.

"I am so sorry," Stansbury posted to social media Wednesday morning. "There is
no one who is more disappointed in myself than me that I was not here the
moment that that gavel dropped."

Pettersen has been less forthcoming. Drop Site reported Tuesday night that
some members had been at an EDW event, and the local Colorado media [pressed
Pettersen](https://x.com/KyleClark/status/2120713677309395256?a=YhFV2V8f-hl_p2W6WxY&s=20)
as to whether she was one of them, but she initially declined to say, allowing
only she had been "denied the ability to vote."

"Her team twice refused to tell us where she was. Our Marshall Zelinger found
that Pettersen was at a Super PAC party," [Local9 News in
Colorado](https://www.9news.com/article/news/local/local-
politics/congresswoman-brittany-pettersen-political-event-missing-hegseth-
impeachment-vote/73-7f0c3b73-ae04-4e4c-8bc8-1460c1805edc) reported.

"Last night I was late to the floor and there is no excuse for that," she said
in a follow-up statement. "I was an Electing Democratic Women [sic] event
celebrating the record-breaking number of new women members who were just
elected, and unfortunately was significantly delayed with the blockade on
Independence Avenue."

The Colorado [local news anchor went
on](https://www.9news.com/article/news/local/local-politics/congresswoman-
brittany-pettersen-political-event-missing-hegseth-impeachment-
vote/73-7f0c3b73-ae04-4e4c-8bc8-1460c1805edc): "So why the hesitancy about
being at an EDW event?" he asked, before explaining: "EDW Action is the Super
PAC for EDW. It took in more than $2.3 million this year from a Super PAC
affiliated with AIPAC, the group that helps elect congressmembers who support
a strong relationship between the U.S. and Israel. Critics describe EDW Action
as a conduit for AIPAC money."

The rest of EDW's executive board includes Reps. **Joyce Beatty** , **Debbie
Dingell** , and **Norma Torres**. Board members include Reps. **Nikki
Budzinski** , **Laura Friedman** , **Julie Johnson** , **Jennifer McClellan**
, and **Jill Tokuda**. (Johnson lost a primary to Justice Democrat **Frederick
Douglass Haynes** in Texas and is not returning to office.)

Frankel [quit the Congressional Progressive Caucus in November
2023](https://theintercept.com/2023/11/20/israel-lois-frankel-progressive-
caucus/) over complaints that the caucus was too critical of Israel; she had
previously been one of just six CPC members to vote to censure Rep. **Rashida
Tlaib** for using the slogan, "From the river to the sea." Earlier this year,
[according to Democratic candidate
](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JZyS1yuaopk)**[Jamie
Belsito](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JZyS1yuaopk)**[,](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JZyS1yuaopk)
Frankel told Belsito that EDW could back her in a Massachusetts primary and
funnel money from AIPAC, AI interests, and crypto companies into her race.
When Belsito objected, saying she didn't want the money whether it was direct
or through a pass-through, EDW endorsed a rival candidate (who lost to
incoming freshman **Dan Koh**).

After the effort to impeach Hegseth failed, Democratic Whip **Katherine
Clark** released a statement claiming, "Republicans just blocked the House
from impeaching Pete Hegseth," calling the GOP "a disgrace" for "protecting an
unqualified, incompetent man over our servicemembers."

Clark, during a meeting of her deputy whips Wednesday,[ told her
colleagues](https://www.ms.now/news/shame-failed-vote-hegseth-impeachment-
democratic-debacle-attendance) they had let the American people down.

She also reportedly noted that seven Republicans also missed the vote, so that
even if Democrats had arrived in time, the GOP had votes to spare they could
add to the board. It's not obvious that her claim is true. Only two of the
seven Republicans who missed the vote won re-election last Tuesday, making it
unlikely they would have been trying to abstain, as members sometimes do, so
as not to face backlash in their districts.
